sections.heading: Client Updates
sections.summary: Lighthouse is prototyping EIP-8411 and attestation bundling; Prysm merged partial columns by default; Lodestar working on partials post-Gloas; Geth published blob protection post.
sections.body:
- **Lighthouse**: preparing for Sepolia fork; reviewing internal networking stack simplifications; continuing prototype work on EIP-8411 and attestation bundling.
- **Prysm**: all partial columns work merged and enabled by default for Fulu and Gloas; observing behavior on the Glamsterdam devnet with no problems so far.
  - Peer scoring and connectivity revamp reviewed and approved, currently soaking on mainnet and Hoodi nodes for ~1 week before merge.
  - New metrics and RPC APIs expose connected peers, bad responses, gossip rejection reasons, connection duration, and agent type; a Grafana-style dashboard will be demoed at next P2P call.
- **Lodestar**: headway on P2P for v1.3; partials coming soon but will not be turned on until after Gloas goes live on mainnet.
- **Geth**: no major networking update; Csaba published a post on blob pool protection mechanisms — adjacent to peer scoring but not peer scoring (half already in Geth, half in a PR); additional hardening on sparse blob pools this cycle.
- **Gattaca (Vlad)**: introduced as an engineering team interested in block propagation on the consensus layer; no updates to share yet.

sections.heading: Gloas Sepolia Bandwidth Profile
sections.summary: X-ray-style bandwidth profiling of post-Glamsterdam Sepolia revealed execution payload timing patterns and a possible Lodestar IDONTWANT bug causing ~60-77 duplicate payload copies.
sections.body:
- Kamil built per-client bandwidth dashboards (Prysm, Lighthouse, Lodestar) using an X-ray-style probe for Sepolia after yesterday's Glamsterdam upgrade.
- Execution payloads appear to propagate right at slot start rather than waiting for attestations, contrary to some expectations; this may differ on mainnet where builders have financial incentives to wait.
  - Builder IDs 1 and 3 attributed to Sigma Prime and Bombora.
  - Discussion in chat noted that some builders may want to wait for attestations to reduce reorg risk before releasing the payload.
- Payload attestation messages use a single global topic; Kamil suggested applying partial-message optimizations (similar to the attestation bundling EIP from Sukun) to payload attestation messages as well.
- **Lodestar bandwidth comparison**: without partial message support, Lodestar's data column sidecar bandwidth is roughly 10× larger than Prysm's for the same block (e.g., ~1 MB vs ~120 KB).
- **IDONTWANT duplicate issue on Lodestar**: Kamil observed 60–77 duplicate copies of execution payload messages (~150 KB each) on Lodestar, compared to 5–10 copies on Lighthouse.
  - Lodestar team confirmed a bug in IDONTWANTs was fixed one or two releases ago; will verify whether the Sepolia-targeted version includes that fix.
- Daniel Knopik has a branch integrating the X-ray probe into Lighthouse (needs rebase); Cayman expressed interest in adding it to Lodestar.
  - Raúl suggested studying the wire protocol and how the Prysm probe hooks into the client to propose a clean integration path for Lodestar.

sections.heading: Discv5 Topic-Based Service Discovery
sections.summary: Felix presented the finalized discv5 topic discovery spec with new REGTOPIC/TOPICQUERY messages; debate on whether CL needs it given ENR-based peer filtering.
sections.body:
- Felix presented the [topic-based service discovery spec](https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/master/discv5/discv5-theory.md#topic-based-service-discovery) and its [Go implementation](https://github.com/datahop/go-ethereum/blob/topdisc/p2p/discover/topicindex/topictable.go).
- The mechanism replaces the original (never-implemented) topic-related message codes in discv5 with new messages: REGTOPIC, REGCONFIRMATION, TOPICQUERY, TOPICNODES.
- Nodes can register arbitrary topic identifiers decoupled from their ENR, enabling targeted search instead of only random-walk discovery.
  - Original motivation: distinguishing testnet nodes from mainnet nodes in the shared DHT.
  - CL use case: finding peers on specific attestation subnets or future subnets.
- The spec is considered final; Geth has an unmerged implementation being evaluated with Datahop via large-scale test runs, still finding minor issues.
- Resource overhead is bounded: each node has a fixed-size index table (e.g., ~10,000 entries); each new node adds capacity, so the system scales with network size.
  - No requirement for all nodes to share the same cache size; can be tuned after deployment.
  - Registration cost is on the registering node; spamming 50,000 topics from one node requires proportional work.
- Incremental deployment is supported: the overlay is somewhat self-maintaining, so not all nodes need to support it initially.
- For very small topics (e.g., 5 nodes out of 15,000), discovery performance is not ideal; works well for topics with a couple hundred participants.
- **Raúl's counterpoint**: for CL needs, peer membership information is already derivable from ENRs (syncnets) or pure functions over peer IDs (attestation subnets); crawling the full network is cheap today (~7-8 MB for all ENRs in memory); topic discovery may be heavy-handed for current CL use cases.
- **Felix's rebuttal**: topic discovery reduces algorithmic search complexity; full-network crawl won't scale long-term; post-quantum ENRs may increase ENR sizes significantly beyond the current ~300-byte cap.
- Raúl acknowledged the post-quantum point and agreed topic discovery is a good baseline capability, especially for third-party overlay services.
- Csaba noted discv5 was deliberately designed as a multi-network protocol, worth keeping in mind.

sections.heading: Decoupled Consensus Simulations
sections.summary: Sukun shared Shadow simulation results for decoupled consensus attestation strategies on 100 nodes; 500-node Cloud Run simulation scheduled for the next day.
sections.body:
- Sukun presented [simulation results](https://hackmd.io/@sukunrt/rkMKx1Eoze) for decoupled consensus attestation propagation strategies, with a 500-node Cloud Run simulation scheduled for the following day.
- **Decoupled consensus background**: 8 slots per round instead of 32; justification after 8 slots, finality after 16 slots; votes split into a finality (FFG) vote and a goldfish vote (for chain head), decoupling the two purposes currently served by a single attestation.
- **Load assumptions**: 2,500 attesters per subnet in simulation (vs ~500 on current mainnet); home nodes would handle ~5,000 attestations per slot (vs ~1,000 today); slightly higher than the expected ~2,000 (4×500) under actual decoupled consensus.
- **Three strategies simulated**:
  1. All FFG votes published at slot start; other traffic flows in parallel.
  2. Staggered publishing: committee split into time buckets (first X% in second 1, next X% in second 2, etc.); nodes hold votes before forwarding if received early; aggregates published at 9 seconds.
  3. Three committees per slot on a single subnet: each committee gets a 4-second window; produces 3 aggregates; equalizes slot traffic profile.
- **Key finding**: when FFG votes all publish at slot start, goldfish votes take >3 seconds due to bandwidth competition with FFG traffic.
  - No good mechanism exists to prioritize between topics on different connections; QUIC stream priorities only work within a single connection.
  - Staggered publishing and multi-committee approaches both significantly improve goldfish vote latency.
- **Shadow simulation setup**: 100 nodes; 20% supernodes (many validators, 1 Gbps), 80% home nodes (1-3 validators).
  - Supernodes tend to connect to each other over time via optimistic mesh shuffling, cutting out low-scoring home nodes; tail latency (P99, max) is dominated by home nodes.
  - Supernode load in simulation is lower than expected on mainnet because supernodes also serve aggregator duties on additional subnets.
- Sukun is integrating a GossipSub tracer for IHAVE/IWANT traffic measurement and plans to make X-ray work with Shadow (Raúl confirmed it should be straightforward).
- **Scaling discussion**: Csaba noted that P2P diffusion scales well (O(log N)) and the current network (~10-12K nodes) is well below the regime where scaling becomes a concern; simulations should focus on stress scenarios (churn, network partitioning, bandwidth constraints) rather than node count.
  - Csaba highlighted that the current stack is slow at building connections (discovery, connectivity ramp-up), which is more likely to be the bottleneck under churn than message propagation scaling.
  - Sukun plans to extrapolate by measuring P95 latency at N nodes and estimating additional hops at larger scales.

sections.heading: EIP-8411: Segmented Payload Broadcast
sections.summary: EIP-8411 (chunking execution payloads into 64 segments) is PFI for Hegota; Lighthouse will implement it regardless; Lodestar raised timing concerns about H-fork scope.
sections.body:
- EIP-8411 is merged in the EIPs repo and PFI for Hegota; it chunks the execution payload into 64 segments and includes a chunks root in the payload bid (a small consensus change).
- **Lodestar's position (Matthew)**: the feature seems technically sound and implementation is straightforward, but questioned the data driving its necessity.
  - Nico (Lodestar) reported no issues with large payload delivery on devnets; no mainnet data yet showing a problem.
  - Primary concern: H-fork scope creep; shipping H quickly is critical because I, J, K forks are existentially important (PQ, execution proofs, etc.); adding complexity risks delaying H past June.
  - Suggested waiting for mainnet data (Feb/March timeframe) before committing, or deferring to I-star when proof propagation also requires similar techniques.
  - Acknowledged the feature is likely needed eventually and that implementation is feasible.
- **Csaba's rebuttal**: testnets lack realistic conditions (no home builders, no bandwidth stress, no scale + adversarial combination); mainnet won't show 200M gas blocks plus blobs plus PQ overhead until it's too late.
  - Simulations use 50 Mbps uplink for home builders (representing residual bandwidth) and 1 Gbps for 20% data center nodes.
  - Segmentation is a well-established networking technique; the EIP is the minimum viable change (no erasure coding yet).
  - The consensus change (chunks root in the bid) is the critical unlock; without it, segmentation is possible but much less optimal.
  - The segmentation parameter could even be set to 1 segment initially, preserving current behavior while having the unlock in place.
  - Networking and research are in co-design: researchers regularly ask for propagation capacity numbers, and having segmentation tools enables better answers.
- **Raúl's view**: networking upgrades don't require lockstep client upgrades (proven with IDONTWANTs, partial messages); segmented propagation is pragmatic, creates immediate headroom, and greases the wheels for larger future proposals (erasure coding on top of chunking).
  - Networking should have a continuous drive to optimize rather than gating on fork boundaries; invest in testing/simulation frameworks to de-risk rolling upgrades.
- **Lighthouse commitment**: João and Daniel confirmed Lighthouse will implement EIP-8411 and attestation bundling with backward compatibility, even if not included in Hegota.
  - Daniel: learning from partial messages feedback, announcing intent upfront so other clients can join; invited Prysm and others to participate.
  - Vlad (Gattaca) gave a thumbs-up in chat.
- Daniel noted in chat: fine to delay to I-star if roadblocks appear, but should attempt in H to avoid deferral cycles.
- Yann noted that since attestation propagation may be revamped in I-star, tackling payload propagation first (in H) makes sense.
- Discussion to continue async on Discord; topic will be raised on an upcoming ACDC call.
